questions.question: Suppose a point source is incident on a system and it produces a beam parallel to the principal axis of the system. The system is

options.text: Either a concave mirror or a convex lens
Either a convex mirror or a convex lens
Two plane mirrors that are perpendicular to each other
Either a concave mirror or a concave lens

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Either a concave mirror or a convex lens**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Concave Mirror:
 
• A concave mirror is a mirror with an inward-curved reflective surface.
 
• When a point source of light is placed at the focal point of a concave mirror, the reflected rays will travel parallel to the principal axis.
 
• This happens because the rays coming from the point source at the focal point reflect off the mirror in such a way that they become parallel after reflection.
 
• So, the concave mirror is able to produce a parallel beam of light when the point source is at its focal point.
 
• Convex Lens:
 
• A convex lens is a lens that is thicker in the middle than at the edges.
 
• If a point source of light is placed at the focal point of a convex lens, the rays passing through the lens will diverge after passing through, but they can be treated as parallel rays on the other side of the lens.
 
• The reason is that the convex lens causes light rays to bend inward (converge) when they pass through it. If the light source is at the focal point, the rays emerging from the lens will be parallel to each other and to the principal axis.
 
• Therefore, a convex lens can also produce a parallel beam of light when the point source is at the focal point.

questions.question: What do you call profits earned by a business firm over and above the opportunity cost of the factor inputs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abnormal profit.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **

__
 
• **Abnormal Profit:**

 
 
• ****Abnormal profit occurs when the firm earns a higher-than-normal profit.****
 
• It occurs when total revenue exceeds total economic costs (implicit costs plus explicit costs).
 
• It is also known as supernormal profit or economic profit which is when a firm's total sales revenue exceeds the total costs of production i.e., they are earning a** profit above and beyond the level of normal profit**.
 
• It is the "profit of a firm **over and above** what provides its owners with a normal (market equilibrium) return to capital that is of the opportunity cost of the factor input."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Normal ****profit:**

 
 
• Normal profit is a profit metric that takes into consideration both explicit and implicit costs.
 
• It may be viewed in conjunction with economic profit.
 
• Normal profit occurs when the difference between a company’s total revenue and combined explicit and implicit costs are equal to zero.
 
 
 
• **Regulated ****Profit:**
 
 
• The optimum profit is the maximum profit level an individual attains.
 
• When the marginal revenue from the sale of a commodity is equal to the marginal cost of production, then an individual is at the optimum profit level.
 
 
 
• **Opportunity costs:**
 
 
• Opportunity costs are the costs of any opportunity a company or business owner didn't take, including rejecting a higher-paying job offer or choosing one return on investment option over another.

• The root hair contains a cell wall made of an outer layer of pectin and an inner layer of cellulose. The function of root hairs is to collect water and mineral nutrients present in the soil and take this solution up through the roots to the rest of the plant. The cell wall is a dynamic structure that determines the shape of the root hair.

• The cytoplasm is made up of water, salts and organic molecules. It is important as it suspends the cell organelles within it. All cells need energy to survive. Root hair cells are alive and therefore need energy, which is why root hair cells contain many mitochondria in them.

• Nucleus is enclosed by a nuclear membrane with pores which allows selective passage of materials into and out of the nucleus. The nucleus contains nucleolus which synthesizes ribosomes and chromatin which contains the cell's genetic material. The nucleus controls all the cell activities, for example it controls the type of enzymes synthesized in the cytoplasm thus regulates the chemical changes which takes place in a cell.

• Their **cytoplasm is thick** and there are not many **tiny vacuoles**. (watery saclike enclosures).

• EI - Nino is a complex weather system that appears once every** three to seven years**, bringing drought, floods and other weather extremes to different parts of the world including India.
 
• The system involves oceanic and atmospheric phenomena with the appearance of warm currents off the coast of **Peru in the Eastern Pacific** and **affects weather in many places including India.**

• However, in some other countries, it may result in a complete reversal, i.e., excessive rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Mitigation of effects:**

questions.question: Two successive discounts of 15% and x% on the sale of an item is equivalent to a single discount of 23.5%. What is the value of x%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

First discount = 15%

Second discount = x%

Equivalent to a single discount = 23.5%

**Concept used:**

Price after successive discounts = Price after single equivalent discount

**Calculation:**

Let the initial amount of the item is Rs.100

First discount price = {15over100 }×100

= Rs. 15

Price after first discount = 100 - 15

= Rs. 85

Second discount price = {xover100}×85

= Rs. 85xover100

Price after second discount = Rs. 85-{85xover100}

We have,

Single equivalent discount of 23.5% = {23.5over100}times 100

= Rs. 23.5

Price after discount = 100 - 23.5

= Rs. 76.5

Now, comparing the value of successive discounts with a single equivalent discount, we get,

Price after second discount = price after one single (23.5%) discount

⇒ 85-{85xover100} =76.5

⇒ 85-76.5={85xover100}

⇒ {8.5over85}×100=x

⇒ x = 10%

Hence, the value of x% is **10%.**

questions.question: A certain percentage of deposits which every bank must keep as ‘reserves’ is called ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is__Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The cash reserve Ratio is a particular minimum amount of the total deposits of customers that needs to be maintained by the commercial bank as a reserve either is cash or as deposits with RBI.
 
• The CRR rate will be fixed as per the guidelines of the Central Bank.
 
• The amount specified as the Cash Reserve Ratio is held or reserved in cash or cash equivalents with RBI.
 
• CRR aims to ensure that banks do not run out of cash to meet their depositors’ payment demands 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Objectives of Cash Reserve Ratio :
 
• A part of the bank’s deposits is with the Reserve Bank of India, it ensures the security of the amount.
 
• It makes it readily available when customers want their deposits back.
 
• CRR helps in keeping inflation under control. At the time of high inflation in the economy, RBI increases the CRR, so that banks need to keep more money in reserves so that they have less money to lend further.
 
• At the time of high inflation, the government needs to ensure that excess money is not available in the economy.
 
• To that extent, RBI increases the Cash Reserve Ratio and the amount of money that is available with the banks reduces.
 
• This curbs the excess flow of money in the economy. When the government needs to pump funds into the system, it lowers the CRR rate, which in turn, helps the banks provide loans to a large number of businesses and industries for investment purposes.
 
• Lower CRR also boosts the growth rate of the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• The cash reserve is either stored in the bank’s vault or is sent to the RBI.
 
• Banks do not get any interest in the money that is with the RBI under the CRR requirements.
 
• If the current CRR rate is 4%, a bank is required to store 4% of the total NDTL or the Net Demand and Time Liabilities in the form of cash.
 
• Statutory Liquidity Ratio or SLR, which can be maintained in either gold or cash, CRR needs to be maintained only in cash.
